scheme2_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Crop insurance to protect farmers against crop loss from natural disasters, pests, and diseases
comparisons.scheme2_value: Free food grain distribution to poor and migrant families for food security

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers (including tenant farmers and sharecroppers) who grow notified crops
comparisons.scheme2_value: Poor families in Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and Priority Household (PHH) categories on ration cards

comparisons.scheme1_value: Financial claim payment (within 2 months) if crops are damaged; affordable insurance premiums (farmer pays 1.5%-5%, government subsidizes rest)
comparisons.scheme2_value: 5 kg free food grain per person per month, on top of subsidized PDS ration

comparisons.scheme1_value: Must own or have legal tenure of land; need land ownership certificate or valid land tenure agreement
comparisons.scheme2_value: No land required; must have a valid ration card in AAY or PHH category

comparisons.scheme1_value: Passport photo, bank passbook, identity proof (Aadhaar/PAN/Voter ID), address proof, land records (RoR/LPC), crop declaration
comparisons.scheme2_value: Ration Card and Aadhaar Card (if linked to ration card)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online via pmfby.gov.in (register as Guest Farmer, fill form, upload documents, pay premium); offline through CSC also available
comparisons.scheme2_value: No application needed. Visit your nearest Fair Price Shop with ration card; authenticate via Aadhaar fingerprint/iris and collect grain

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online (primary) and offline via Common Service Centers (CSC)
Must apply within ~2 weeks of the start of each sowing season (Kharif/Rabi); missing this cuts off coverage for that season
comparisons.scheme2_value: No seasonal deadline; grain distributed monthly through Fair Price Shops on ongoing basis

comparisons.scheme1_value: Covers 50+ notified crops in notified areas only; natural disasters, pests, diseases, post-harvest losses (14 days max), prevented sowing (up to 25% indemnity)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Covers all AAY/PHH families across India; wheat allocated to 6 states/UTs, rice to remaining states

comparisons.scheme1_value: Only notified crops in notified districts covered; varies by state and crop
comparisons.scheme2_value: All states/UTs covered; One Nation One Ration Card allows migrants to collect grain anywhere in India

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmer pays 1.5%-5% of sum insured depending on crop type; government subsidizes 80%-98.5%; NE states/J&K/Himachal get 100% government payment
Losses from farmer negligence, non-compliance with practices, outside crop cycle, from non-notified areas, or if premium unpaid; losses beyond thresholds not covered
comparisons.scheme2_value: Only AAY and PHH categories eligible (general ration card not enough); grain type depends on state allocation

comparisons.scheme1_value: Claims targeted within 2 months of harvest; uses satellite imaging, drones, and mobile apps for loss estimation
comparisons.scheme2_value: No claim process; grain collected monthly at Fair Price Shops with no waiting period

comparisons.scheme1_value: If you are a farmer worried about crop loss from disasters, pests, or weather
comparisons.scheme2_value: If you are a poor or migrant family on a ration card needing food assistance

recommendation: These are two completely different schemes serving different needs. **Choose PMFBY if:** You are a farmer growing notified crops and want insurance against crop loss — apply before the seasonal cut-off (usually 2 weeks from sowing start). **Choose PMGKAY if:** You are a poor or migrant family with an AAY or PHH ration card and need free monthly food grains — visit your Fair Price Shop with your ration card, no application needed. **Important:** This is AI-guided information only, not official notification. Always verify eligibility at pmfby.gov.in or nfsa.gov.in and consult your nearest agricultural office (for PMFBY) or block administration (for PMGKAY) for final decisions.
